preconditions: Identify the operation, instance lifetime, task/context and how the executing caller uses proposals.
Supply nonnegative token counts and a suitable budget; record each actual execution once.
Retain complete source data before using partial compression helpers and verify receiver state.

expected_effects.effect: route and estimate helpers produce advisory tiers and estimated token/cost values without model calls or writes.
expected_effects.scope: Caller-provided text, in-memory mappings, budget/cache state and returned proposal.
expected_effects.basis: Task mapping or explicit force_tier chooses the desired tier; a recent matching cache key returns FREE. Budget failure may downgrade or return a LOCAL fallback.
expected_effects.impact: local_available describes tier eligibility, not discovered hardware. A fallback does not enforce the token cap or establish a usable backend.
expected_effects.verification: Exercise explicit FREE and exhausted budgets in isolated instances; verify actual feasibility separately in the execution layer.

expected_effects.effect: record and Budget.spend increment usage; report aggregates the caller-supplied history.
expected_effects.scope: Budget counters, CallRecord history and returned totals in the current Python objects.
expected_effects.basis: No date rollover, persistence, reservation or deduplication is implemented. report uses a rough fixed premium cost per recorded call.
expected_effects.impact: Repeated records double-count usage; a new instance forgets previous spend. Estimated comparisons can differ from actual provider billing.
expected_effects.verification: Compare counters with known recorded calls and real execution IDs; independently measure target usage before interpreting savings.

expected_effects.effect: cache_response retains response references and evicts the oldest stored timestamp beyond 500 entries.
expected_effects.scope: Instance-local cache keyed by caller-supplied string; route lookup uses task type and input text with a 24-hour age check.
expected_effects.basis: set retains data without copying; lookup ignores model, project, system prompt, requested tier and current source state.
expected_effects.impact: Caller mutation and omitted context can change or invalidate apparent reuse; the proposal does not authenticate the answer.
expected_effects.verification: Inspect caller key/context, age, shared object references and invalidation rules before treating a hit as useful.

expected_effects.effect: AgentCompressor retains a shared knowledge map and size history and returns partial field/list transformations.
expected_effects.scope: In-memory knowledge references, returned data and recursively appended transmission counters.
expected_effects.basis: compress omits known fields/list members; decompress merges dictionaries and replaces other values. No messages or files are sent.
expected_effects.impact: List reconstruction, deletions, reordering and nested shared keys can lose data or retain stale state. Size counters are character estimates and count recursive calls.
expected_effects.verification: Compare reconstruction with full source data, especially lists and deletions; retain originals and actual receiver knowledge.

downstream_effects.effect: An executing caller may treat a proposal or a cost report as evidence of availability, capacity or savings.
downstream_effects.scope: Downstream model routing, billing decisions and usage reports.
downstream_effects.basis: The returned labels and estimates are advisory, and counters only reflect explicit calls to record/spend.
downstream_effects.impact: Unavailable local fallback, undercounted concurrent work or stale usage can lead to failed work or overspend.
downstream_effects.verification: Require actual endpoint checks and recorded provider usage from the executing layer before claiming feasibility or savings.

downstream_effects.effect: Consumers can act on incomplete or stale cached/compressed information.
downstream_effects.scope: Agent context, reconstructed state and subsequent decisions.
downstream_effects.basis: Cache context is narrow and compression assumes shared receiver knowledge without acknowledgement.
downstream_effects.impact: Information loss can propagate to later decisions even after the in-memory helper is discarded.
downstream_effects.verification: Compare target outputs against the complete source and verify the target task independently.

reversibility.strategy: Rebuild object state from a caller-owned snapshot or replay verified records once; restore full source data for context. Reconcile downstream actions separately.
residual_effects: Lost source state may be unrecoverable without retained originals.
Discarding an object does not undo requests or decisions already performed by consumers.

retry.check_before_retry: Read-only estimates can be repeated against stable state; record/spend double-count and cache/compression writes alter timestamps, references or history. Reconcile partial caller actions first.
retry.stop_condition: Resolve unknown accounting state, cache context or receiver knowledge before repeating mutations or using their output for execution.

required_scope: Existing task authority for the supplied data and in-memory state. This helper neither performs nor authorizes model requests, message sending or budget commitments by downstream callers.

analysis.summary: A stdlib advisory routing/accounting helper with explicit in-memory mutations. Budget naming and nominal tier values do not imply persistent quotas, live availability or measured savings.
uncertainties: Caller-supplied usage is not authenticated; counters are not transactionally shared across threads/processes.
Tier rates and the premium baseline are static heuristics, not current provider prices.
AgentCompressor lacks lossless reconstruction guarantees and the cache omits execution context.
Downstream callers and runtime state are outside these local source bindings.

reuse.target: Compare advisory tier policies in an offline routing experiment.
reuse.rationale: Pure estimates and caller-recorded usage can be replayed with isolated objects before involving endpoints.
adaptations: Scope objects and cache keys to complete target context; implement calendar/persistence or reservations in the caller when needed.
Use comparable measured token counts and independent quality checks rather than nominal tier values.
reuse.validation: Compare explicit tiers, exhausted budgets, repeated recording and representative task outputs against actual target usage and availability.
